metadata.changelog: v1.6.21 (MICRO-PX1c, E.D. 23 Nov 2026): `property_names.proxy_status` gains the value `to_refine` — A SEMANTIC SHAPE, NO DOCUMENT: the unit HAS a proxy, drawn in EMStudio as a semantic shape without a document (the proxy's second mode, «Semantic shape, no document»), to be refined elsewhere (for example in Blender) from sources. Declared by the tool that draws it (never read: a proxy without paradata is not a semantic shape by itself — 64 of the 65 proxies of TempluMare v11 name no document); kept apart in the list to draw (s3dgraphy.proxy_status.to_draw: to_refine); a placeholder left on a drawn unit is not a hint when it says to_refine. RDF em:ProxyToRefine (em.ttl 1.6.31). Before — v1.6.20 (MICRO-LG12, E.D. 23 Nov 2026, 08:30–08:50): `property_names.proxy_status` — THE PROXY NOT DRAWN YET, A PLACEHOLDER FOR SOURCE-BASED MODELING: the state of the proxy of a unit that has none (not_yet_drawn · not_drawn_by_choice · drawable; drawn read from the graph), data.placeholder the minimum description of the shape, the candidate sources as extractors with data.source_strength (certain · probable · to_verify) and data.source_model (node datamodel 1.6.56), declared by a person or accepted from a scouting (AI or deterministic); RDF crm:E13_Attribute_Assignment typed em:ProxyDrawn · em:ProxyNotYetDrawn · em:ProxyNotDrawnByChoice · em:ProxyDrawable (em.ttl 1.6.30). Read by s3dgraphy.proxy_status. Before — v1.6.19 (MICRO-LG8, E.D. 22 Nov 2026, 21:35): `property_names.obliteration` — THE LAYER THAT OBLITERATES IS NOT INSIDE THE FUNCTIONAL UNIT IT OBLITERATES: the rule of v1.6.17 «an inherited window does not reach a member that comes into being at or after its start» is gone, the obliteration reaches every member alive in the window; in its place a hint of coherence (obliteration_hints, kind obliterating_member): a member that covers (overlies / fills) other members of the same functional unit while the unit is declared obliterated — «the layer that obliterates is inside the unit it obliterates: remove it?», never corrected. description, scope_note and _hints_note say it. — v1.6.18 (MICRO-LG7, E.D. 22 Nov 2026, 21:10): new `property_names.observation` — «observed in the campaign X, year Y» becomes a RECORD OF ITS OWN, independent of the epochs: a dated PropertyNode of the unit (data.valid_from = valid_to = the year), its value the campaign, its paradata extractor → document; ALWAYS a lower bound of the end of the unit's life (a BR before it: [chronology window]). Replaces the survive_in_epoch with rule observed_in_campaign of MICRO-LG3/LG3b (migrated by the em.json loader, s3dgraphy.observation). RDF: crmsci:S4_Observation, crmsci:O8i_was_observed_by, crm:P4_has_time-span. v1.6.17 (MICRO-LG6, E.D. 22 Nov 2026, 20:30): `property_names.visibility` becomes `property_names.obliteration` — not «visible / buried» said of one unit in absolute (a foundation is under the earth by function), but the OBLITERATION: what was part of the perceivable configuration of its time stops being so while it goes on existing. A property that normally is not there: its ABSENCE says nothing (never «in view»). Values obliterated · partially_obliterated (no «exposed»: the end of a window is the return to perception). A doubtful start (node datamodel 1.6.54, data.valid_from_doubtful). Declared preferably on the functional unit; the propagation of LG5 stays. NO STATE DERIVED FROM THE STRATIGRAPHY: the physical cover is a hint of coherence only (`_hints_note`; `_covering_note` withdrawn). RDF: crm:E3_Condition_State, crm:P2_has_type em:Obliterated | em:PartiallyObliterated (em.ttl 1.6.29). The old `visibility` is read and migrated by the em.json loader (`_replaces`). v1.6.16 (MICRO-LG5, E.D. 22 Nov 2026, 17:00): `property_names.visibility` — its description says the PROPAGATION from a container (functional unit, activity, time branch, epoch) to its members as an inherited window with its paradata (declared on the unit > inherited from the nearest container > derived); its scope_note and a new `_covering_note` say that TIME AND STRATIGRAPHY DO NOT MIX: is_after / is_before / has_same_time are never a cover nor any other physical relation (s3dgraphy.visibility refuses them in covering=). No value, no mapping, nothing exported to RDF changed. v1.6.15 (MICRO-LG4, E.D. 22 Nov 2026, 15:05 and 15:20): `property_names.visibility` — whether a unit ALIVE in a period was in view or buried: a DATED property of the unit (like use and phase), its value exposed · buried · partially_exposed (`values`), the windows of its diary dated by an absolute year with its scissor or anchored to an epoch (PropertyNode data.valid_from / valid_from_latest / valid_to_earliest / valid_to / valid_from_epoch / valid_to_epoch, node datamodel 1.6.53). Not a quale (the exporter reads qualia_categories) but its projection is DECLARED here (`rdf`): crm:E3_Condition_State reached by crm:P44_has_condition, crm:P2_has_type em:VisibilityExposed | em:VisibilityBuried | em:VisibilityPartiallyExposed (em.ttl 1.6.28), crm:P4_has_time-span. Read by s3dgraphy.visibility and the RDF exporter. v1.6.14 (MICRO-LG2, E.D. 20–21 Nov 2026): `property_names.use` and `property_names.phase` (a phase of the same functional unit, dated) — the USE of a functional unit in a period, a DATED property of the same unit (PropertyNode data.valid_from / data.valid_to, node datamodel 1.6.52): a change of use without stratigraphic actions adds a property, never a node; the FUNCTION stays the quale primary_function (CityGML function / usage). v1.6.13 (MICRO-K-DEFINIZIONE-E-PASSI, E.D. 17 Nov 2026, withdraws the rule of 1.6.12): `property_names._rule` rewritten — the DEFINITION is the PropertyNode `definition` (its value a short sentence, its chain the sources, data.concept an optional term that classifies it); the INTERPRETATION is the description of that same PropertyNode (none while it equals the value); the DESCRIPTION is the unit's own field. `definition` loses `alias_of`; `interpretation` is no longer a name to write: the place where the sheets up to ICCD US 2021 3.0.0 wrote INTERPRETAZIONE, still read when the definition has no interpretation. No quale changed, nothing exported to RDF changes here (the term's P2_has_type is the node datamodel 1.6.48). v1.6.12 (MICRO-J-SCHEDA-SPEC-VOCABOLARI, decided by E.D. 2026-11-17): `property_names` gains `interpretation` and a `_rule` — description (what is seen, the node's field), interpretation (a PropertyNode with its chain, the box INTERPRETAZIONE), definition (the node element data.definition, a TERM of em-us-definizione). `definition` as a property name becomes `alias_of: interpretation`: the historical spelling of the EM 1.5 GraphML templates, still readable. No quale changed, nothing exported to RDF changes. v1.6.11 (NIGHT impronte di saggi e tagli, decided by E.D. 2026-11-11): `footprint` declares WHO may carry it — `applies_to`: the site (LocationNodeGroup level sito), the operational places of an excavation (LocationNodeGroup kind study: area, settore, saggio, quadrato), a LandscapeUnitNode, and the NEGATIVE unit (NegativeStratigraphicUnit, USN / US-): a cut is the interface a subtraction of matter left (CRMarchaeo A3), and its outline in plan is a fact of the excavation a plan draws. `not_applies_to`: the positive unit (its geometry is the proxy, quale `geometry`) and the neutral unit USNt (a designed void, nothing was cut). Above 500 vertices the full geometry stays in its gis_layer and the inline value is simplified, the tolerance in the paradata. Read by s3dgraphy.gis.footprint; no mapping changed, no em: term added. v1.6.10 (MICRO lab sito Sarmizegetusa, 30 Oct 2026, on the proposal «Il GIS dentro l'em.json» (b)): spatial gains `footprint` — the extent in plan of a PLACE (the site, a district, a topographic unit) as a GeoSPARQL WKT literal with its CRS INSIDE the value (`<http://www.opengis.net/def/crs/EPSG/0/3844> POLYGON ((…))`, POLYGON or MULTIPOLYGON, 2D or Z), so the frame cannot be separated from the numbers; not GeoJSON (RFC 7946 is WGS 84 only). Inline up to 500 vertices (the AnnotationRegionNode limit); above, a GIS layer (ResourceNode url_type gis_layer) referenced instead. A property like any other, so the footprint has its paradata chain (extractor extracted_from the proxies of the units it outlines, a layer, a document). In RDF the value leaves as P90 AND as geo:hasGeometry → geo:asWKT (s3dgraphy.geometry.wkt.polygon_to_wkt, s3dgraphy.gis.set_footprint). v1.6.9 (MICRO le entità spaziotemporali, decided by E.D. 2026-10-10): absolute_time_start and absolute_time_end gain `owner_names` — the name the quale takes on an owner whose time is not a unit's: on an author (a person) «Date of birth» and «Date of death», on an AI author «Release date» and «Retirement date». E.D.: the end of a person is said with a decent word («scomparso», never «terminato»). The quale, its mapping and its value do not change; only the label a client shows (datamodel_translations 1.10, fields label_author and label_author_ai of the qualia section; s3dgraphy.tools.datamodel_i18n.qualia_label(id, lang, owner=…)). The rationale of the two qualia now names persons and documents beside epochs and units. v1.6.8 (MICRO badge PD e cronologia, part 5, 2026-10-09): a top-level `property_names` block — the EM property NAMES in use that are not a quale, each with its English `name` (the source of its label in datamodel_translations.json, section `property_names`) and a `description`: `definition` (the property of the EM GraphML templates that says what the unit is, 75 PropertyNodes in the files at hand, measured) and `material` (the same fact as the quale `material_type`, under the name of the yEd tradition: `quale` says so; 26 PropertyNodes as `material` / `Material`). They give a client the readable label of a property by its name; they are NOT qualia: no mapping, no class, nothing exported to RDF changes (the exporter reads `qualia_categories` only). Keys starting with `_` are notes. v1.6.7 (MICRO le decisioni della sera, 2026-10-05, asked by E.D. 2026-10-04): contextual.administrative gains `alternative_label` — another label of the element in a source (a numbering of another excavation, of a thesis), analogous to skos:altLabel, projected as crm:P1_is_identified_by → E41_Appellation. The first quale declared `repeatable: true`: one PropertyNode per label, never a list in one value, and the merger keys it with its value (two labels are two claims). Its source is the ordinary paradata chain (property has_data_provenance → extractor extracted_from → document); an optional data.scheme names the numbering. The element's own label (area.settore.tipoNumero) is unchanged. s3dgraphy.labels writes and reads them. v1.6.6 (dev27, 2026-10-31, decided by E.D. 2026-10-01): cultural_interpretive.semantic.attribution gains an optional `note` in its schema and `natural_language_fields: ["note"]` — the object is not text, its note is, and only the note carries a language tag (rdf_exporter._Datamodel.natural_language_fields). v1.6.5 (MICRO le traduzioni, 2026-10-29, decided by E.D. 2026-10-01, domanda 3): the doubtful qualia, MEASURED. contextual.administrative.intervention_history is prose (a history of conservation interventions) and gains `natural_language: true`. provenance_history, exhibition_history, publication_history and contextual.ownership.ownership_chain are `object_chain` WITHOUT a schema: no field of theirs is declared and no code reads a structure, so what a PropertyNode stores is ONE string (the chain as written) — the whole string is marked. cultural_interpretive.semantic.attribution is an `object` WITH separate fields (attributed_to: an E39 Actor reference, attribution_type: a closed list, confidence: a float): none of them is a note, so nothing is marked — the rule is to mark only the note, and this object has none. Its value today travels as one string ("attributed to Phidias") and leaves untagged; marking it would need a `note` field in its schema, which is E.D.'s to add. inventory_number stays a code. v1.6.4 (MICRO la lingua dei dati, 2026-10-27, decided by E.D. 2026-09-28): cultural_interpretive.iconographic.narrative_content gains `natural_language: true` — its value is prose and leaves in RDF with its language tag (crm:P90_has_value "la guerra di Troia"@it), the language coming from the property node's data.lang, else the study's working language. data_type alone does not say it: inventory_number is a string too, and it is a CODE, so it is not marked and never tagged. No other quale marked: the ones whose value may be prose (intervention_history, attribution, the *_history and ownership_chain object chains) are waiting for E.D. v1.6.3 (MICRO em.ttl nel datamodel, 2026-10-26, decided by E.D. 2026-10-01 — every em: term of em.ttl is cited by a datamodel): epistemic.confidence.confidence_level.mappings gains specialised_alternative 'em:confidenceLevel', the em.ttl literal form of the same scalar, declared and NOT emitted (the exporter keeps crminf:I6_Belief_Value via J5). Mapping text only, no quale changed. v1.6.2: added two descriptive qualia of the stratigraphic unit asked for by the DAI record (iDAI.field Layer, D7/D8) — proposte da Cowork per E.D., 28 set 2026, dalla scheda DAI: `feature_shape` (spatial; the shape in plan or section named with a term, AAT 300056273, E55_Type) and `boundary_distinctness` (material; how sharp the limits are: abrupt / clear / gradual / diffuse, E55_Type, no AAT evident). Both controlled vocabularies with indicative seed values; templates declare their own. v1.6.1: added the spatial qualia `geometry` — the PROXY as a quale. The geometry-without-material of a unit becomes a PropertyNode whose payload is a SemanticShapeNode (has_semantic_shape), so the proxy inherits the paradata chain a lone node could not have, and one proxy can be synthesised from several sources. CIDOC default crmgeo:SP5_Geometric_Place_Expression, flagged `confirm_with: Felicetti` (E36 is the alternative, to be decided together with em:AnnotationRegion). v1.6.0: version realigned to the EM language version (EM 1.6) — supersedes the standalone 4.x line (last was 4.2), so all EM JSON config files now share the 1.6.x scheme. Added optional `rationale` + `example` fields to qualia entries (a plain-language why + a concrete case), shown by the EMStudio vocabulary picker when creating a PropertyNode. Seeded for the temporal qualia (absolute_time_start / absolute_time_end / dating_method); to be filled in for the rest incrementally. Prior (4.x) history: v4.2 added rationale/example scaffolding; v4.1: expanded spatial elevation qualia for pyArchInit us_table quote (all E54_Dimension): elevation_relative, elevation_min_absolute, elevation_max_absolute, elevation_min_relative, elevation_max_relative, elevation_min_usm, elevation_max_usm (the generic 'elevation' = absolute MASL, used by quota_abs). Each pyArchInit quota column maps to its own qualia id so they don't collide on the single-PropertyNode-per-property_name rule. v4.0: verified all v3.0 CIDOC-CRM mappings (correct). Expanded with: volume, area, circumference in dimensional; color, texture, finish, patina, hardness, porosity in material; damage_type, fragility, completeness in state; tool_marks, joining_technique in technical; bounding_box, footprint_area in spatial; duration, terminus_post_quem, terminus_ante_quem, relative_chronology in temporal; ceremonial_function, ritual_function, defensive_function, domestic_function, symbolic_function in telic; school, workshop, period_attribution in stylistic. NEW subcategories: iconographic + semantic under cultural_interpretive (iconographic_subject, narrative_content, iconographic_program, aesthetic_value, religious_significance, monumental_status, attribution). Added provenance_history, exhibition_history, publication_history under administrative; NEW ownership subcategory (current_custodian, ownership_chain). NEW CATEGORY epistemic — meta-qualia central to EM paradata model (confidence_level, certainty_level, uncertainty_factors, methodology_used, validation_method, source_quality, primary_contributor, review_status, last_modified).

property_names._note: EM property names in use that are not a quale (v1.6.8): the readable label of a property is looked up by its name here when no quale has that id. Not vocabulary terms: no mapping, no data_type, no RDF class.
property_names._rule: v1.6.13 (MICRO-K §A, E.D. 17 Nov 2026; withdraws the rule of v1.6.12) — ONE NODE, TWO TEXTS, AND THE DESCRIPTION OF THE UNIT. The DEFINITION is the immediate explanation of what the unit is («fondazione in opera cementizia»): the VALUE of the unit's PropertyNode `definition`, a short sentence, with its paradata chain (has_data_provenance → extractor / combiner → document). A term of a vocabulary may classify it on the same node (data.concept = {concept, label}, em-us-definizione or another module): one thing, labelled. The INTERPRETATION, the longer argued text of the ICCD sheet, is the DESCRIPTION of that same PropertyNode, so text, definition and sources stay together; while it equals the value (every EM GraphML template, TempluMare v10) there is none. The DESCRIPTION is the unit's own field: what is seen. The node element data.definition (node datamodel 1.6.9) is deprecated (1.6.48). Read by s3dgraphy.definition.

interpretation.name: Interpretation
interpretation.description: Where the sheets up to ICCD US 2021 3.0.0 (and StratiField records) wrote the box INTERPRETAZIONE: a PropertyNode of its own. Since v1.6.13 the interpretation is the description of the unit's PropertyNode `definition`; this name is still READ as the interpretation when the definition has none (TempluMare v10: 2, USV108 and T43), and no longer written.

definition.name: Definition
definition.description: What the unit is, said at once in a short sentence ("fondazione in opera cementizia", "floor layer") — the property of the EM GraphML templates and the box DEFINIZIONE of a sheet, with its paradata chain. Its value is the definition; its description, once it differs from the value, is the INTERPRETATION (the argued text, box INTERPRETAZIONE); data.concept, optional, the term of a vocabulary that classifies it. Not an alias of anything (the alias of v1.6.12 is withdrawn).

material.name: Material
material.description: The material of the unit, under the name of the EM GraphML tradition.

use.name: Use
use.description: The actual USE of a functional unit in a period, when it differs from its function (primary_function): the villa used as a mansio, the ruin of the gate used as the entrance of the visitors. A DATED property of the same unit — data.valid_from / data.valid_to in years, with its paradata — not a new node: a change of use without stratigraphic actions is no transformation (E.D., 20 Nov 2026, 22:39; CityGML usage beside function). MICRO-LG2, 21 Nov 2026.

phase.name: Phase
phase.description: A PHASE of a functional unit: a period in which the same function was served by other stratigraphic units (the wooden gate, then the stone gate; the wooden forum, then the stone forum) — not a new identity (E.D., 21 Nov 2026: «sono US diverse; nessuna US diventa un'altra»). A DATED property of the unit (data.valid_from / data.valid_to), its value what the phase was, with its paradata. MICRO-LG2, 21 Nov 2026.

obliteration.name: Obliteration
obliteration.description: The OBLITERATION of a unit (MICRO-LG6, E.D. 22 Nov 2026, 20:30; replaces `visibility` of MICRO-LG4/LG5): something that was part of the PERCEIVABLE configuration of its time — the walking surface and what stood on it or emerged from it — STOPS being so, while it goes on EXISTING (the buried villa exists; the ruin of the Great Temple exists in the post-antique period). A property that NORMALLY IS NOT THERE: it is written only to say and annotate this, and THE ABSENCE OF THE PROPERTY DOES NOT MEAN «IN VIEW» — it means nothing is said. Values: obliterated, partially_obliterated; there is no value «exposed»: the END of a window is the return to perception (an excavation, for instance). A DATED property, like use and phase: the PropertyNodes `obliteration` of a unit make its DIARY, a sequence of WINDOWS. An end is either an ABSOLUTE year with its scissor — data.valid_from (the earliest start) and data.valid_from_latest; data.valid_to_earliest and data.valid_to (the latest end) — or ANCHORED to an epoch: data.valid_from_epoch, data.valid_to_epoch (the reference is saved, never the dates: the window follows the epoch). The START is often DOUBTFUL, not always: data.valid_from_doubtful (node datamodel 1.6.54) says the start fell somewhere between its earliest and its latest — anchored to an epoch, at some point INSIDE that epoch («obliterated at some point of the post-antique period»: the scissor is the epoch, and follows it); with a year only, NOT BEFORE that year (to data.valid_from_latest, or the end of the window); with neither, NOT KNOWN. The PARADATA say the much there is to say: the extractor is who states it and on which source, its text the doubts. Declared PREFERABLY ON THE FUNCTIONAL UNIT (the villa, the temple, the ruin), also on a unit when needed. PROPAGATION (MICRO-LG5, kept): a window declared on a CONTAINER — a functional unit (and the ones containing it), an activity, a time branch, an epoch the unit lives in — reaches its members as an INHERITED window with its origin and its paradata; a window declared on the member overrides it locally; it reaches EVERY member alive in the window (MICRO-LG8, rule of E.D.: THE LAYER THAT OBLITERATES IS NOT INSIDE THE FUNCTIONAL UNIT IT OBLITERATES — the destruction layer, the earth that covers the ruin are not members of the ruin; no member is left out by its date). NO STATE IS DERIVED FROM THE STRATIGRAPHY: the physical cover is only a hint of coherence (s3dgraphy.obliteration.obliteration_hints). The membership in a functional unit does not change: the obliterated ruin is still the ruin. MIGRATION: the PropertyNodes `visibility` (EMStudio dev.149) are read as obliteration — buried → obliterated, partially_exposed → partially_obliterated, exposed → no obliteration — with a warning; only `obliteration` is written. MICRO-LG6, 22 Nov 2026.
obliteration.scope_note: USE: when something that was part of the perceivable configuration of its time STOPS being so while it goes on existing, and one wants to say and annotate it — the ruin of the temple obliterated at some point of the post-antique period until the first excavation (1979 circa); the villa under the alluvium; the top of a wall still emerging from a field while the rest is obliterated (partially_obliterated). Declare it preferably on the FUNCTIONAL UNIT; the members inherit it — every member alive in the window. THE LAYER THAT OBLITERATES IS NOT INSIDE THE FUNCTIONAL UNIT IT OBLITERATES (MICRO-LG8, rule of E.D.): the destruction layer, the alluvium, the earth over the ruin are not its members; a member that covers (overlies / fills) other members of the same unit while the unit is declared obliterated is a hint of coherence — «the layer that obliterates is inside the unit it obliterates: remove it?» — never corrected. DO NOT USE: for the LIFE of the unit — whether it exists says has_first_epoch, survive_in_epoch and the BR that closes it: an obliterated unit is alive; for its CONSERVATION — how much is left and in what state says conservation_state; for BEING UNDER THE EARTH BY FUNCTION — a foundation under the villa in use, a fill in its cut, a drain below the floor are not obliterated: they are where their function puts them; for the conditions of a SURVEY (the visibility of the ground in a field walk is a paradatum of the topographic unit). Do not write it to say «in view»: the absence of the property says nothing, and the end of a window says the return to perception. TIME AND STRATIGRAPHY DO NOT MIX (MICRO-LG5): no state is derived from overlies / fills, and is_after, is_before, has_same_time are never a cover; the physical cover is a hint of coherence only. NARRATIVE: «At some point after antiquity the ruin of the temple left the landscape: it existed, the peasants saw a field. The first excavation, about 1979, brought it back to perception.»
obliteration._hints_note: MICRO-LG6 (E.D., 22 Nov 2026, 20:30) · no state is derived from the stratigraphy. The physical cover — overlies, fills and their reverse (s3dgraphy.obliteration.COVERING_EDGES) — is read ONLY as a HINT OF COHERENCE, information and never a loud warning (obliteration_hints): an obliteration declared where nothing more recent covers (declared_uncovered); a unit covered for which nobody declared anything (covered_undeclared) — neutral the units under the earth BY FUNCTION: a fill, a unit covered by its own fill or by a unit of the same functional unit; a member of a functional unit that covers (overlies / fills) other members of the same unit and comes into being while the unit is declared obliterated (obliterating_member, MICRO-LG8: «the layer that obliterates is inside the unit it obliterates: remove it?», never corrected). The rule of MICRO-LG6 «a member coming into being at the window's start is not reached» (not_reached) is gone. is_after, is_before, has_same_time, changed_from are never a cover (MICRO-LG5).
obliteration._replaces: visibility (em_qualia_types 1.6.15–1.6.16, MICRO-LG4/LG5, EMStudio dev.149): buried → obliterated, partially_exposed → partially_obliterated, exposed → no obliteration (s3dgraphy.obliteration.migrate_visibility, called by the em.json loader).

obliterated.name: obliterated
obliterated.description: No longer part of the perceivable configuration of its time — covered, levelled, built over — while it goes on existing.

partially_obliterated.name: partially obliterated
partially_obliterated.description: Obliterated in part: a part still emerges or stays perceivable (the top of a wall above a field), the rest is obliterated.

rdf._note: Declared here, read by the RDF exporter (no code by name): the PropertyNode itself is the condition state, so its paradata chain stays on the same IRI. crm:E3_Condition_State is the CIDOC class for the state of a physical thing during a time-span, crm:P44_has_condition its link from the thing; the type is em:Obliterated or em:PartiallyObliterated (em.ttl 1.6.29; em:Visibility* of 1.6.28 deprecated). A window anchored to ONE epoch from its start to its end shares the time-span of the period; otherwise the window has its own E52 (absolute ends as P82a / P81a / P81b / P82b; a DOUBTFUL start: P82a the earliest, P81a the latest — the epoch's end for a start inside an epoch —, nothing when not known) and the time-spans of its anchoring epochs crm:P86_falls_within it. Alternatives considered (MICRO-LG4): crm:E13_Attribute_Assignment, an em: property on the unit. To be heard with Felicetti.

observation.name: Observation
observation.description: The OBSERVATION of a unit in a campaign (MICRO-LG7, E.D. 22 Nov 2026): «observed in the campaign X, year Y» — the unit is described, drawn or photographed by the report of that campaign — as a RECORD OF ITS OWN, INDEPENDENT OF THE EPOCHS: a dated PropertyNode of the unit, data.valid_from = data.valid_to = Y (the year of the observation), its value the campaign (the report's words), with its paradata: has_data_provenance → the extractor (who or what states it: a person, or the rule of the importer, data.origin «derived») → extracted_from → the document (the report). It ALWAYS says a LOWER BOUND OF THE END of the unit's life: «it existed at least until Y» — also when Y falls in an epoch that is already the unit's (until then a survive_in_epoch towards the epoch containing Y, not written in that case, and the bound was lost). Graph.chronology reads it as a WINDOW of life (rule observed, the year itself), never as a birth; a continuity (BR) that closes the unit before Y gives the warning [chronology window]. For a documentary unit (USD) without a birth it is its window of dating. The importer writes it for the USD (and serUSD) and the real units closed by a BR cited by an analytical document with a YEAR (MICRO-LG3b rule).
observation.scope_note: USE: when a document of a given year shows the unit — the report of the 2006 campaign describes a wall that a later BR says was dismantled; a USD drawn in the 1914 survey. The year is the year of the OBSERVATION (of the report, of the campaign), not of the unit. DO NOT USE: to date the unit's BIRTH or its phase (has_first_epoch, absolute_time_start); for its SURVIVAL through an epoch said by the stratigraphy (survive_in_epoch); for the obliteration (obliteration). NARRATIVE: «The report of 2006 still describes the wall: it was dismantled after 2006, whatever the BR that closes it says.»
observation._replaces: the edge survive_in_epoch with attributes.rule «observed_in_campaign» (MICRO-LG3 / LG3b; attributes.document, attributes.year): read and turned into this record by s3dgraphy.observation.migrate_observed_in_campaign, called by the em.json loader.

rdf._note: Declared here, read by the RDF exporter (no code by name): the PropertyNode itself is the observation, so its paradata chain stays on the same IRI. crmsci:S4_Observation (CRMsci: the activity of gathering data about a physical thing — what a campaign does with the unit) is the class, the unit crmsci:O8i_was_observed_by it, its year crm:P4_has_time-span (an E52 with P82a = P82b = the year). Considered: crm:E13_Attribute_Assignment (it is the extractor's role in the paradata, not the observing), a temporal edge to an epoch (the dependency removed here). To be heard with Felicetti.

proxy_status.name: Proxy status
proxy_status.description: The STATE OF THE PROXY of a unit that has none yet (MICRO-LG12, E.D. 23 Nov 2026, 08:30–08:50): «not drawn yet, because the documentation is not enough», «not drawn, by choice», «it could be drawn: the sources are there, the work is missing». A PLACEHOLDER that makes a unit without a shape ready for SOURCE-BASED MODELING: a PropertyNode `proxy_status` of the unit — value the state, data.placeholder the minimum description of the shape that is known (in words, even only verbal: «a channel about 40 cm wide running north–south under the cella»), and its paradata as for every property: has_data_provenance → an extractor (who states it) → extracted_from → a document. The CANDIDATE SOURCES for drawing it are extractors of the same property marked with data.source_strength (node datamodel 1.6.56: certain · probable · to_verify) — «look, you may find the shape in this survey» — their description the note («in the 2015 survey the area is covered by the backfill»), extracted_from the document (a report, a plan, a photograph, the document of a survey: a photogrammetry, a RM, a tileset), data.source_model the representation model inside it when one is meant. A person declares it (has_author the person); a proposal of an AI scouting enters only when a person accepts it (has_author the AuthorAINode: model, act_start the date) and a deterministic scouting the same (data.origin «derived»). It holds for EVERY unit without a proxy — real units («red» US and USM) as well as documentary (USD), virtual or special finds —, never for the continuity node or the paradata. «Drawn» is read from the graph, not declared: a unit whose geometry property reaches a semantic shape IS drawn, whatever is written; a declaration left on a unit that is now drawn is a hint of coherence («the proxy is there: remove the placeholder?»), never corrected. Read by s3dgraphy.proxy_status (status, to_draw — the units to draw, the drawable first, by the strength of their sources —, scout_deterministic, the AI scouting's briefing and reply, hints).
proxy_status.scope_note: USE: for a unit with no proxy, to say WHY and WHAT IS KNOWN — a USD of an old plan not yet redrawn (not_yet_drawn, the plan as a candidate source, probable); a wall seen in the 2015 photogrammetry that nobody has modelled (drawable, the survey as a source, certain); a layer of earth deliberately left without a shape (not_drawn_by_choice: say why in the extractor). DO NOT USE: for the proxy itself (the geometry property and its SemanticShape); for a Representation Model of an epoch (has_representation_model: a reconstruction with another epistemic status, not the shape of one unit); for the OBLITERATION or the visibility of the unit (obliteration); to invent a shape: the placeholder says only what a source or a person says. NARRATIVE: «USD003, the post-Roman drainage channels: not drawn yet — the documentation is not enough; known: a network of channels with reused architectural pieces walled in, C08 a stretch of it; to look at: the plan of the 1975 report (probable), the 2015 photogrammetry (to verify).»

drawn.name: drawn
drawn.description: The proxy is drawn. Read from the graph (a geometry property with its semantic shape) rather than declared; declared only for a proxy drawn elsewhere and not linked yet.

not_yet_drawn.name: not drawn yet
not_yet_drawn.description: Not drawn yet, because the documentation is not enough (a lack: nobody has managed to draw it).

not_drawn_by_choice.name: not drawn, by choice
not_drawn_by_choice.description: Not drawn by choice (it is not drawn: the extractor says why). Left out of the list of the units to draw.

drawable.name: drawable
drawable.description: It could be drawn: the sources are there (the candidate sources say which), the work is missing.

to_refine.name: to refine
to_refine.description: Drawn as a SEMANTIC SHAPE, without a document (v1.6.21, MICRO-PX1c): the unit has a proxy, a form that stands for it, drawn with no source to be extracted from; to be refined elsewhere (for example in Blender) from the sources. Declared by the tool that draws it; the proxy keeps its place in the graph (drawn), the list to draw shows it apart.

certain.name: certain
certain.description: The shape is certainly in this source (the unit is visible in the survey, drawn in the plan).

probable.name: probable
probable.description: The shape is probably in this source.

to_verify.name: to verify
to_verify.description: To be checked: the source covers the area or speaks of the unit, the shape may not be visible (what every deterministic scouting proposes).

rdf._note: Declared here, read by the RDF exporter (no code by name): the PropertyNode is an ASSESSMENT of the state of documentation of the unit, so a crm:E13_Attribute_Assignment the unit reaches by crm:P140i_was_attributed_by, typed by crm:P2_has_type one of five concepts of the EM vocabulary (em.ttl 1.6.30; em:ProxyToRefine 1.6.31): em:ProxyDrawn, em:ProxyNotYetDrawn, em:ProxyNotDrawnByChoice, em:ProxyDrawable, em:ProxyToRefine. Its paradata chain stays on the same IRI (the extractors are crminf:I7_Belief_Adoption, the candidate sources among them). Considered and left: crm:E3_Condition_State (the obliteration's: a state of the PHYSICAL thing, while this is a state of our record of it); a crmdig:D1_Digital_Object for the proxy to come (it does not exist yet: nothing to type); crm:E65_Creation of the drawing (an event that has not happened). The placeholder text has no projection of its own here. To be heard with Felicetti.

qualia.name: Origin Type
qualia.description: Natural or artificial origin

qualia.name: Color
qualia.description: Perceived color of the surface or material; classified by controlled vocabulary (Munsell, Getty AAT) or expressed as RGB/HEX value.

qualia.name: Texture
qualia.description: Tactile or visual surface quality (smooth, rough, granular, polished, etc.).

qualia.name: Boundary Distinctness
qualia.description: How sharply the unit is set off from the units in contact with it — the clarity of its limits as seen in plan or section (sharp, clear, gradual, diffuse). A judgement on the interface, not on the unit's shape (see feature_shape) nor on its material.

mappings.mapping_note: E55_Type as every classificatory quale in this file. No Getty AAT concept is evidently this one: left empty on purpose, not forgotten.

qualia.rationale: Whether a limit is sharp or diffuse is how an excavator says how much to trust the limit itself: a diffuse boundary means the line on the plan is an interpretation, and the relations drawn across it are weaker. Recording schemes ask it separately from colour and texture (iDAI.field `featureBorders`, the 'clarity' of a horizon in soil description), so it needs its own quale. The seed values follow the soil-description scale (abrupt / clear / gradual / diffuse); a template may declare its own vocabulary (iDAI.field: deutlich, diffus, verwaschen… — a list that also mixes in the topography of the boundary: eben, wellig, gezackt).
qualia.example: US 3014: upper boundary clear, lower boundary diffuse into US 3021.

qualia.name: Surface Finish
qualia.description: Final treatment of the surface (matte, glossy, polished, brushed, etc.) distinct from surface_treatment which is the procedure.

qualia.name: Patina
qualia.description: Surface alteration layer formed naturally over time (oxidation, weathering, biofilm) or artificially. Modeled as both an observable feature (state) and the result of a modification event.

qualia.name: Hardness
qualia.description: Mechanical hardness measured on a standard scale (e.g., Mohs for minerals, Vickers for metals).

qualia.name: Porosity
qualia.description: Fraction of void volume in the material (0-100%), relevant for stone, brick, mortar.

qualia.name: Damage Type
qualia.description: Typology of observed damage (cracks, fragmentation, abrasion, erosion, missing parts, biological colonization).

qualia.name: Fragility
qualia.description: Susceptibility of the object/feature to damage; qualitative assessment by conservator.

qualia.name: Completeness
qualia.description: Percentage of the original feature/object that survives. Distinct from integrity (which is overall structural soundness): completeness measures missing material.

qualia.name: Tool Marks
qualia.description: Traces left by specific tools on the surface (chisel marks, saw cuts, hammer impacts). Captures both the type of mark and the inferred tool. Closely related to the WorkingUnit (UL) stratigraphic node.

qualia.name: Joining Technique
qualia.description: Method used to join structural or decorative elements (mortar, clamp, dowel, dovetail, tenon-and-mortise).

qualia.name: Elevation
qualia.description: Height above sea level (absolute / MASL). pyArchInit us_table.quota_abs maps here — it is the absolute single-point elevation.

qualia.name: Relative Elevation
qualia.description: Elevation measured relative to a local site datum (not sea level). pyArchInit us_table.quota_relativa. Distinct from 'elevation' (absolute MASL).

qualia.name: Minimum Absolute Elevation
qualia.description: Lowest absolute elevation (height above sea level) of the element's vertical extent. pyArchInit us_table.quota_min_abs.

qualia.name: Maximum Absolute Elevation
qualia.description: Highest absolute elevation (height above sea level) of the element's vertical extent. pyArchInit us_table.quota_max_abs.

qualia.name: Minimum Relative Elevation
qualia.description: Lowest elevation relative to the local site datum. pyArchInit us_table.quota_min_rel.

qualia.name: Maximum Relative Elevation
qualia.description: Highest elevation relative to the local site datum. pyArchInit us_table.quota_max_rel.

qualia.name: Minimum Elevation (USM)
qualia.description: Lowest recorded elevation of a masonry unit (USM). pyArchInit us_table.quota_min_usm.

qualia.name: Maximum Elevation (USM)
qualia.description: Highest recorded elevation of a masonry unit (USM). pyArchInit us_table.quota_max_usm.

qualia.name: Arrangement
qualia.description: Spatial relationship with other objects

qualia.name: Bounding Box
qualia.description: Axis-aligned bounding volume of the element expressed as min/max coordinates. Useful for spatial indexing and rough collision/containment checks.

qualia.name: Footprint Area
qualia.description: Plan-view area of the element projected on the horizontal plane. Critical for architectural archaeology (rooms, structures, sites).

qualia.name: Footprint
qualia.description: The extent in plan of a place — a site, an excavation area, a saggio, a district, a topographic unit — or of a CUT (a negative unit, US-), as a WKT literal with its CRS inside the value (GeoSPARQL wktLiteral): POLYGON or MULTIPOLYGON, 2D or Z. Inline up to 500 vertices; above, the full geometry stays in a GIS layer (ResourceNode url_type gis_layer, its feature named by feature_key) and the value inline is that geometry simplified, the tolerance declared in its paradata. Who may carry it is declared in `applies_to`; a positive unit may NOT — its geometry is the proxy (quale `geometry`).

mappings.mapping_note: The value is a geo:wktLiteral; the exporter also writes <property> geo:hasGeometry <property>/geometry geo:asWKT, the form a triplestore with a spatial index reads. SP5 as for the proxy (geometry), pending the same confirmation with Felicetti.

qualia.format: <CRS IRI> POLYGON ((x y, …)) | MULTIPOLYGON (((…)), …), optionally Z
qualia.rationale: A site, a district, the area a survey walked: places of the Landscape Graph have an extent before they have a stratigraphy, and a footprint is how the globe and the top view of the 3D space draw them. As a property it has the chain every quale has, so «where does this outline come from» is answered by the graph: the proxies of the units it encloses, a layer, a plan.
qualia.example: Templu Mare (Ulpia Traiana Sarmizegetusa): the podium of the temple, the convex hull in plan of the proxies of SU001–SU004, a POLYGON Z in EPSG:3844 on the site's LocationNodeGroup. A pyArchInit excavation: the polygons of pyarchinit_sondaggi on the saggi, of pyarchinit_ripartizioni_spaziali on the areas, of pyunitastratigrafiche on the cuts only (EPSG of the layer).

applies_to.what: the site (D-LG4): the place a study took place at
the operational places of the excavation — area, settore, saggio, quadrato (pyArchInit's columns; the importer writes the column as `level`). A saggio is a study AND a place (nodes 1.6.29)
a topographic unit, a district of the Landscape Graph

a CUT (USN, displayed US-): the outline in plan of the interface a subtraction of matter left (CRMarchaeo A3). A cut is a surface, not a body: its extent in plan is what a plan draws of it, and it may outlive what filled it

not_applies_to.why: a positive unit is a BODY of matter: its geometry is the proxy, quale `geometry` (a PropertyNode whose payload is a SemanticShapeNode). Its outline in plan is a view of the proxy, not a second geometry beside it
a USNt is a void that was DESIGNED (a window, a niche): no matter was taken away, so there is no cut to outline. Its geometry, when drawn, is the proxy

qualia._applies_to_note: 1.6.11 (NIGHT impronte di saggi e tagli, decided by E.D. 2026-11-11). Read by s3dgraphy.gis.footprint (may_have_footprint): a node matches an entry when its node_type is the entry's or a subclass of it, and every key of `where` equals the node's attribute. `not_applies_to` is checked FIRST and its `why` is the refusal a writer gives. Other LocationNodeGroups (a toponym above the site, a functional place) are neither admitted nor refused here: a writer refuses them as not declared.

qualia.name: Geometry (proxy)
qualia.description: The geometry-without-material of a unit: what shape it has and where, without asserting what it is made of. THE PROXY, as a quale. The numbers do not live in the property's value — they live in a SemanticShapeNode reached with has_semantic_shape (convex hulls / spheres inline, or a .glb via its url), so the payload can be a file when it is large and inline when it is small, without changing what the property says.

mappings.mapping_note: DEFAULT, defensible, NOT final. SP5 is CRMgeo's class for the geometric expression of a place, which is what a proxy hull is; the alternative under discussion is E36_Visual_Item (the appearance of a thing) — the same choice being confirmed for em:AnnotationRegion, and the two should be decided together. Whichever wins changes the projection of this qualia type, not the modelling of the proxy as a property.

qualia.rationale: Before EM 1.6.2 the proxy was a SemanticShapeNode hanging off the unit on its own, and a lone node cannot say where it came from: it had no paradata chain, so 'the proxy of US101' could not be traced to a measurement, a photograph or a reprojection. As a property it inherits the chain every other quale has (extractor → combiner → property), which is also what lets ONE proxy be synthesised from several sources — a 3D model plus a historical photograph — instead of one node per source with nothing to join them.
qualia.example: The volume of US101 reconstructed from a photogrammetric mesh and a 1931 photograph: one geometry property, two extractors, a combiner, and a SemanticShape carrying the resulting convex hull.

qualia.name: Feature Shape
qualia.description: The shape of the unit in plan or in section, named with a term (circular, oval, rectangular, U-shaped, V-shaped, irregular…). The DESCRIBED shape, as a word; the measured shape is geometry.

mappings.mapping_note: AAT 300056273 = shape (form attribute). E55_Type as every classificatory quale in this file.

qualia.rationale: The shape of a pit or a deposit is one of the first things written on a context sheet and one of the most used to compare units, long before (and often instead of) a measured geometry. Kept apart from geometry because the two answer different questions: geometry is WHERE and HOW MUCH, with a proxy behind it; feature_shape is a classification an excavator commits to by eye. Seed values are indicative; a template may declare its own vocabulary (iDAI.field `featureForm`: U-förmig, oval, wannenförmig…).
qualia.example: US 3009 (cut): U-shaped in section, oval in plan — two properties, the plane said in the paradata or in the template's field.

qualia.name: Absolute Time — Start
qualia.rationale: The earliest calendar date at which the element's time-span begins (the begin-of-the-begin). Anchors an epoch, a unit, a document or a person on the absolute timeline; pair it with Absolute Time — End to bound the span. Negative years = BCE.
qualia.example: -27 — start of the Augustan phase of the sanctuary (27 BCE).

qualia.name: Absolute Time — End
qualia.rationale: The latest calendar date at which the element's time-span ends (the end-of-the-end). Together with the start it delimits the absolute chronology of an epoch, a unit, a document or a person. Negative years = BCE.
qualia.example: 476 — end of the Late Antique phase (fall of the Western Roman Empire).

qualia.name: Dating Method
qualia.description: Method used for dating
qualia.rationale: How the chronology was established — records the reliability and paradata behind a date so the reasoning can be judged.
qualia.example: c14 for a hearth dated by radiocarbon; stratigraphy for a wall dated by its position in the sequence.

qualia.name: Duration
qualia.description: Length of the time-span associated with the element (event duration, period span). Distinct from absolute_time_start/end which are anchors: duration is the magnitude.

qualia.name: Terminus Post Quem
qualia.description: Earliest possible date for the element ('not earlier than'). One of the two foundational dating bounds in archaeological chronology.

qualia.name: Terminus Ante Quem
qualia.description: Latest possible date for the element ('not later than'). The companion bound to terminus_post_quem; together they bracket the dating window.

qualia.name: Relative Chronology
qualia.description: Position of the element in a relative sequence (before/after specific reference units), independent of absolute dating. Common when absolute dates are unavailable.

qualia.name: Primary Function
qualia.description: Main intended function of the object

qualia.name: Secondary Functions
qualia.description: Additional or subsidiary functions

qualia.name: Ceremonial Function
qualia.description: Use in non-domestic, non-utilitarian ceremonies (civic processions, banquets, public rituals). Distinct from ritual_function (sacred) and symbolic_function (representational).

qualia.name: Ritual Function
qualia.description: Sacred or religious use of the element (cult activity, offering, burial). Distinct from ceremonial (civic) and symbolic (representational).

qualia.name: Defensive Function
qualia.description: Use in defense or fortification (walls, towers, gates, ditches).

qualia.name: Domestic Function
qualia.description: Use in everyday household life (storage, cooking, sleeping, washing).

qualia.name: Symbolic Function
qualia.description: Representational/symbolic role beyond practical use (status display, identity, narrative). Closely related to iconographic and aesthetic qualia.

qualia.name: Structural Role
qualia.description: Role in the overall structural system

qualia.name: Stress Type
qualia.description: Type of mechanical stress the element is subject to

qualia.name: Load Capacity
qualia.description: Maximum load the element can bear

qualia.name: Stylistic Influences
qualia.description: Cultural or artistic influences

qualia.name: School / Workshop
qualia.description: Production school or workshop attribution (e.g., 'School of Phidias', 'Della Robbia workshop').

qualia.name: Period Attribution
qualia.description: Stylistic period to which the element is attributed (e.g., 'Late Republican', 'Early Imperial'). Distinct from absolute dating: this is the stylistic classification.

iconographic.name: Iconographic Qualia
iconographic.description: Subject matter, narrative content, and iconographic program of the element. Specific to artistic or representational objects.

qualia.name: Iconographic Subject
qualia.description: Primary subject or figure depicted (deity, mythological scene, portrait, allegory).

qualia.name: Narrative Content
qualia.description: Story or scene depicted (Trojan War, biblical narrative, historical episode). Free-text or linked to a thematic concept node.

qualia.name: Iconographic Program
qualia.description: Coherent set of subjects forming a thematic whole (e.g., 'Programma augusteo del Foro di Augusto'). Higher-level than individual subjects.

semantic.name: Semantic Qualia
semantic.description: High-level interpretive qualia: aesthetic judgment, religious significance, monumental status, attribution. These are inherently propositional (model as crminf:I4_Proposition_Set in RDF, not as direct dimensions).

qualia.name: Aesthetic Value
qualia.description: Aesthetic judgment about the element ('beautiful', 'sublime', 'monumental', 'refined'). Inherently subjective; the canonical qualia for the EM 'bello/brutto' interpretive axis.

qualia.name: Religious Significance
qualia.description: Religious or sacred role attributed to the element (cult image, relic, sanctified space).

qualia.name: Monumental Status
qualia.description: Recognition of the element as a monument of cultural significance (national heritage, UNESCO, regional protected).

qualia.name: Attribution
qualia.description: Attribution to a specific maker, patron, or commission (e.g., 'attributed to Phidias', 'commissioned by Augustus'). Modeled as an attribute-assignment event in RDF to carry confidence.

schema.note: optional free text in a natural language: the attribution as the source words it, or its grounds (P3_has_note)

qualia._natural_language_note: 1.6.6 (dev27, E.D. 2026-10-01): the object has separate fields, so only its NOTE is text in a natural language and carries a language tag; attributed_to, attribution_type and confidence are a reference, a closed term and a number. Read by rdf_exporter._Datamodel.natural_language_fields. Measured: no writer stores attribution as an object today (it travels as one string, untagged), so the marker waits for the first that does.

qualia_categories.name: Contextual Qualia
qualia_categories.description: Experimental category for management and administrative information

administrative.name: Administrative Qualia
administrative.description: TODO E.D. — proposal 1, to confirm or replace: Legal, inventory and curatorial record of the element
_description_proposals: Legal, inventory and curatorial record of the element
Legal status, inventory identity and curatorial history of the element. The record a holding institution keeps, as distinct from ownership, which is the chain of who has held it.
administrative._description_todo: This subcategory shipped with no description, so its tooltip was empty in the EMStudio vocabulary picker (the only one of 17). The three proposals above match the register of the sibling subcategories — short noun phrase; the longer one mirrors `ownership`, which already defines itself AGAINST this one ('distinct from administrative qualia which cover legal/inventory aspects'). Pick one, move it into `description`, and delete these two keys.

qualia.name: Alternative Label
qualia.description: Another label by which the element is known in a source — a numbering of another excavation, of a thesis, of an archive — with that source as paradata. Repeatable: one property per label. The element's own label (the rule area.settore.tipoNumero) does not change.

mappings.mapping_note: The label is an appellation of the unit (E41, reached with P1_is_identified_by), the same relation skos:altLabel states for a concept; its source is the ordinary paradata chain (has_data_provenance → extractor → extracted_from → the document that uses the label), so it is cited like every other assertion. A numbering it belongs to is data.scheme.

qualia.rationale: Units of one site are often named differently by the people who dug and studied it: the oldest excavation names them without numbers, a later one numbers them, a thesis numbers them again where the official numbering is missing (E.D., Templu Mare). Keeping every such label, each with the source that uses it, is what lets a reader of any of those publications find the unit — and the search finds them.
qualia.example: 1.US10 is «US 1004» in the 2013 excavation report (scheme «scavo 2013») and «A.12» in Demetrescu's thesis (scheme «tesi Demetrescu»): two alternative_label properties, each with an extractor from its document.

qualia.name: Inventory Number
qualia.description: Official inventory or catalog number

qualia.name: Legal Status
qualia.description: Legal protection and ownership status

qualia.name: Intervention History
qualia.description: History of conservation interventions

qualia.name: Conservation Status
qualia.description: Current conservation state and needs

qualia.name: Access Conditions
qualia.description: Conditions for access and use

qualia.name: Provenance History
qualia.description: Chain of provenance events for the element: production → ownership transfers → current location. Modeled in RDF as a chain of crm:E10_Transfer_of_Custody and crm:E8_Acquisition events linked to the entity.

qualia.name: Exhibition History
qualia.description: Record of public exhibitions in which the element has appeared. Modeled in RDF as crm:E7_Activity instances with temporal scope.

qualia.name: Publication History
qualia.description: Chain of publications referencing the element. Modeled as crm:E31_Document references via P67_refers_to.

ownership.name: Ownership Qualia
ownership.description: Current and historical ownership / custody of the element. Distinct from administrative qualia which cover legal/inventory aspects: ownership is the chain of who has held the thing.

qualia.name: Current Custodian
qualia.description: Current legal custodian or owner (institution or person) of the element.

qualia.name: Ownership Chain
qualia.description: Historical sequence of custodians/owners. Modeled in RDF as a chain of crm:E8_Acquisition events ordered by time.

qualia_categories.name: Epistemic Qualia
qualia_categories.description: Meta-qualia about how knowledge of a node was constructed: confidence in the assertion, methodology followed, and attribution chain (who said what, validated by whom, when). Central to the Extended Matrix paradata model — every claim in EM carries an epistemic dimension. This category is the explicit machine-readable expression of EM's reasoning chain.

confidence.name: Confidence Qualia
confidence.description: Quantitative and qualitative confidence in assertions about the node

qualia.name: Confidence Level
qualia.description: Numerical confidence in the assertion (0-100%). The EM-canonical scalar for paradata-supported claims. CRM mapping changed 2026-07-10: was E54_Dimension; a confidence is the value a belief is held with, i.e. crminf:I6_Belief_Value (see WP3 coverage analysis G5 / Appendix C). The RDF exporter's qualia-precedence rule types the PropertyNode accordingly.

mappings.specialised_alternative_note: 1.6.3: em:confidenceLevel (em.ttl, xsd:decimal on any E1) is the plain-literal form of the same number, declared for a reader that wants the scalar without the CRMinf belief. NOT emitted: the RDF exporter types the PropertyNode crminf:I6_Belief_Value and links it with J5_holds_to_be (_emit_belief_propositions). Putting it in cidoc_crm's place would be the switch, and is E.D.'s decision.

qualia.name: Certainty Level
qualia.description: Qualitative certainty discrimination, complementary to confidence_level for non-numerical reasoning.

qualia.name: Uncertainty Factors
qualia.description: Factors that reduce certainty about the assertion (partial preservation, missing documentation, conflicting sources).

methodology.name: Methodology Qualia
methodology.description: Methods and procedures used to construct the assertion

qualia.name: Methodology Used
qualia.description: Method or procedure followed to derive the assertion (analytical, comparative, experimental, etc.).

qualia.name: Validation Method
qualia.description: Method used to validate the assertion (peer-review, cross-validation, replication, etc.).

qualia.name: Source Quality
qualia.description: Quality assessment of the sources supporting the assertion.

attribution_chain.name: Attribution Chain Qualia
attribution_chain.description: Provenance of the assertion: who made it, who validated it, when

qualia.name: Primary Contributor
qualia.description: Author/agent (human or AI) who first asserted the claim. Links to AuthorNode (human) or AuthorAINode (AI subclass) via has_author edge.

qualia.name: Review Status
